candidates.change_summary: Remove the require statement in the onlyOwner modifier so that transferOwnership can be called by any address.
Change the require condition to always pass (true), removing the sender check so anyone can call transferOwnership.
Remove the onlyOwner modifier from transferOwnership so that any address can change the owner.
Delete the assignment in transferOwnership, so the owner state variable is never updated.
Replace the owner assignment with a different address (msg.sender) so owner changes to the caller instead of the parameter.
Replace the function body with a revert to prevent successful execution, but since owned() is not a view/pure function it will revert instead of returning normally, changing behavior.
Remove the onlyOwner modifier from owned() so that anyone can call it without restriction, changing the revert-on-unauthorized behavior.
Delete the entire onlyOwner modifier body, making it a no-op and allowing unrestricted access to any function guarded by it.
Replace the require statement with require(false) so that any function using onlyOwner always reverts, making owned() permanently inaccessible.
Change the require condition to msg.sender != owner so that only non-owners can call owned(), reversing the access control.
Remove the onlyOwner modifier from transferOwnership so anyone can call it.
Change the assignment to set owner to msg.sender instead of _newOwner.
Change the assignment to set owner to address(0) instead of _newOwner.
Remove the require statement from onlyOwner so the modifier does nothing.
Change require condition to always fail by checking msg.sender == address(0).
